scope: Prove local HTTP transport-disconnect cancellation while a native resume parser child is active, including child termination/reaping and preservation of profile, uploaded resume bytes, and extraction history.

evidence.summary: A real loopback TCP client sent the extraction request and half-closed its request transport while the parser child was running. The server observed disconnect; the actual child process was killed and reaped; durable operation readback was CANCELLED; profile and resume bytes remained unchanged; no new revision was persisted.
58 focused unit, integration, and connected Chromium browser tests passed.
TypeScript check and Vite production build passed.

evidence.command: python -m tools.verification.agent_skills; python -m tools.verification.catalogue; python -m tools.verification.progress validate; python -m tools.coordination.lane_coordination validate; git diff --check; python -m compileall -q tests/integration/test_profile_import.py
evidence.summary: All repository validators, lane validation, whitespace validation, and test-module compilation passed.

limitations: The half-closed client cannot consume an HTTP response; this test therefore asserts transport observation and durable cancellation state. Existing simulated Request-disconnect coverage separately asserts the route's HTTP 499 result.

This evidence covers native resume parsing only. Other external-operation categories, live ATS/provider runtimes, and other process classes remain outside this acceptance slice; issue #5 remains OPEN/PARTIAL.
No schema changed; PostgreSQL/Docker migration checks are not applicable to this test-only slice.
